title: Heritage Advisors and Sheikh Sultan bin Jassim: one Qatari fund across three stories
summary: The fund's three documented roles hold up. Heritage Advisors / Sheikh Sultan bin Jassim paid EPA chief Lee Zeldin's consultancy in 2023, holds about 15% of Newsmax through a disclosed SEC ownership chain (~19.7M shares, worth ~$1.6B at the March 2025 listing against ~$50M invested), and paid $45M for a quarter of Fred Daibes's Edgewater holdings in the Menendez case. The new layers are a Daily Beast report that the Heritage-Daibes entity controls co-defendant Wael Hana's IS EG Halal site, and a single anonymous-sourced Free Beacon claim tying Sheikh Sultan to Hamad bin Jassim, reported prior owner of the Qatari Air Force One jet. No source shows coordination among the threads or any US government benefit: we found no EPA matter involving Qatar, Newsmax is suing Trump's FCC rather than benefiting from it, and Daibes's $1M Javelin pardon bid failed.

sub_claims.statement: Heritage Advisors is Sheikh Sultan bin Jassim Al Thani's vehicle, and its Newsmax stake sits in a disclosed US ownership chain (Naples Investment Holdco LLC -> Heritage Investments LP -> Heritage GP -> a trust of which he is sole beneficiary).
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (SEC filing as relayed by filing aggregators; sec.gov itself could not be fetched here). A Form 3 filed around 1 May 2025, after Newsmax's 31 March 2025 NYSE listing, shows Naples Investment Holdco LLC holding 19,737,553 Class B shares. Heritage Investments LP is Holdco's sole member, and Sheikh Sultan is sole beneficiary of the Heritage Trust at the top of the chain. ICIJ/WaPo (March 2024) reported the stake had earlier been moved into a Cayman Islands structure. Measured against Ruddy's 39.24M shares (about 30.4%), Holdco's block is roughly 15% of outstanding shares. That is our arithmetic, and it matches a Forbes-based 15% figure relayed by a low-authority ownership site. At the first-day close of $83.51 the block was worth about $1.65B, against the roughly $50M paid in 2019-20; this is also our arithmetic. The stock fell sharply afterwards, and we did not establish the current value or any sale after the 29 September 2025 lockup expiry.

sub_claims.statement: The same fund was the 'Qatari Investment Company' in the Menendez case, closing a $45M deal for a quarter stake in Daibes's Edgewater properties, and the joint entity controls the base of Wael Hana's IS EG Halal.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED for the deal; the IS EG overlap is SINGLE-SOURCE. The superseding indictment (January 2024) alleges Menendez introduced Daibes to a royal principal of a Qatari investment company, which signed a letter of intent and in 2023 formed a joint venture with a Daibes company to invest tens of millions in a New Jersey project. Trial documents and press identify the fund as Heritage Advisors (NYT, Real Deal, FDD). FDD, citing property records, says Heritage finalized a $45M deal with Daibes in December 2022. The Daily Beast reports that this bought a one-quarter stake in Daibes's Edgewater properties through a joint entity, Hudson Edgewater Associates. According to the Daily Beast, that entity controls the site that serves as IS EG Halal's base of operations; IS EG Halal is co-defendant Wael Hana's company in the Egypt strand of the same case. Heritage's lawyers say Sheikh Sultan had no relationship with IS EG and did not know about the overlap until the outlet asked. Neither Sheikh Sultan nor Qatar was charged.

sub_claims.statement: A former Biden aide arranged the 2021 meeting between Menendez, Sheikh Sultan and Qatari official Ali Al Thawadi.
sub_claims.finding: SINGLE-SOURCE investigative reporting (ICIJ, July 2024), based on an email to a Menendez staffer. The aide, identified as Doyle, told ICIJ he set up one meeting as a favour to a friend, was not paid, and disclosed his role to law enforcement. OpenSecrets data cited by ICIJ show he gave Menendez $2,900 about six weeks later. The meeting was in 2021, before Trump's second term. This layer shows the fund's access-seeking was bipartisan; it is not a Trump link.

sub_claims.statement: Sheikh Sultan is a confidant and business partner of Hamad bin Jassim (HBJ), the former Qatari PM reported to be the prior owner of the 747-8 (P4-HBJ) that Trump accepted as Air Force One.
sub_claims.finding: SINGLE-SOURCE (Washington Free Beacon, May 2025; anonymous 'source familiar'). From flight records and social media, the Free Beacon ties the tail numbers P4-HBJ and A7-HJJ to HBJ and says P4-HBJ is the jet slated for Trump. It identifies Sheikh Sultan as an HBJ confidant and business partner. The NYT, as relayed by the Free Beacon, reported that P4-HBJ was registered with charter firm Global Jet Isle of Man, whose official would not name the current owner. This is the only source we found that joins the Heritage/Menendez thread to the jet. The Sultan-HBJ partnership is not documented in any filing we saw. C73 had only the headline.

sub_claims.statement: Lee Zeldin was paid by Heritage Advisors in 2023, before joining the administration, and divested his consulting firm under his ethics agreement.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (OGE 278e; Jewish Insider; The Intercept). Heritage Advisors (London) is listed as a client of Zeldin Strategies, with compensation above $5,000 for April-December 2023. Zeldin said the work required no FARA registration and that he never lobbied or did media work for the firm. E&E News reports he drew $775,000 in salary from Zeldin Strategies overall. His 2025 ethics agreement commits him to divest the firm and to recuse from EPA matters involving his wife Diana Zeldin's clients, since she works there; this is per search excerpts, as OGE PDFs could not be fetched here. Whether Heritage stayed a client after his confirmation is not established. His 2026 annual 278e (signed 13 May 2026) exists, but we could not read its entries. Per Quincy, the Heritage engagement began shortly after a 2023 Newsweek op-ed in which Zeldin criticised Qatari influence.

sub_claims.statement: Any EPA matter involving Qatari interests during Zeldin's tenure.
sub_claims.finding: NOT FOUND. Searches of Qatari state media (QNA, The Peninsula) and US coverage turned up no Zeldin trip to Qatar, no meeting with Qatar's environment ministry, no LNG-related EPA action naming Qatar, and no Zeldin role in the May 2025 Doha visit. No source alleges any EPA action benefiting Heritage or Qatar.

sub_claims.statement: Newsmax's dealings with the administration: favourable treatment?
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED, and it cuts against a capture narrative. (a) FCC: in March 2026 Newsmax joined DirecTV, cable groups and public-interest groups in suing to block the FCC Media Bureau's 19 March 2026 approval of the Nexstar-Tegna merger. The challengers cited Trump's February Truth Social endorsement and Chair Carr's support. In July 2026 the D.C. Circuit dismissed the challenge for lack of jurisdiction over a bureau-level order, not on the merits. (b) Pentagon: Newsmax got Pentagon workspace in Hegseth's February 2025 rotation, but in October 2025 it refused his new press rules and turned in its badges, and in December 2025 it was among outlets denied briefing access. (c) The defamation settlements were private: Smartmatic $40M (Axios, March 2025) and Dominion $67M (AP, August 2025). Neither involved the government. (d) Commercial: Trump Media's Truth+ carries Newsmax (C21). The documented relationship is commercial carriage plus Ruddy's personal closeness to Trump. We found no FCC or other federal benefit to Newsmax.

sub_claims.statement: Heritage Advisors' other investments: Fort Partners (Miami), The News Movement, Indy Eleven.
sub_claims.finding: Fort Partners is DOCUMENTED: Sidley Austin announced on 29 June 2023 that it advised Heritage Advisors, 'led by HE Sheikh Sultan bin Jassim Al Thani', on an add-on investment in the privately held Miami real-estate firm; no amount was given. The News Movement is SINGLE-SOURCE (ICIJ, March 2024): Heritage invested in it, a Gen Z news startup co-founded by Will Lewis, who became Washington Post publisher in January 2024. Newsmax's spokesman pointed to this when the Post reported the Newsmax stake. Indy Eleven is SINGLE-SOURCE plus a database entry: ICIJ cites a 'professional soccer team in Indiana', and PitchBook lists Heritage Advisors (UK) as a minority investor in Indy Eleven. Club announcements name a different 'Heritage' (Jeff Laborsky's Heritage Group), so this needs checking. ICIJ also lists a Miami developer, consistent with Fort Partners. We found no Heritage investment with a Trump-family business.

sub_claims.statement: Daibes paid Javelin Advisors (Keith Schiller) $1M for a pardon bid, and Menendez himself sought a Trump pardon; neither got clemency.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (LDA filings via NBC; three sources). Daibes paid $1M in Q1 2025 to Schiller and Javelin for 'executive relief' from his seven-year sentence (sentenced January 2025). His lawyer said the engagement ended in June 2025. Menendez lobbied publicly for a Trump pardon before reporting to prison in June 2025. NYT (January 2026, via New Jersey Globe) reported Trump was not considering it. We found no clemency for Menendez, Daibes or Hana through November 2026. No source says Heritage or Sheikh Sultan had any role in Daibes's pardon effort.

sub_claims.statement: Any source connecting the Zeldin, Newsmax and Menendez/Javelin threads to each other.
sub_claims.finding: PARTLY. Accountable.US and FDD/Courage.Media place Zeldin's client and the Menendez-case fund side by side as the same entity, which is a documented identity. The Free Beacon alone adds the HBJ/jet layer. No outlet alleges that Heritage's payment to Zeldin, its Newsmax stake, or its Daibes deal were coordinated, or that any of them produced a US government action. The three-story chain remains our cross-referencing.

corrections: C73 gives the Newsmax stake only as the ~$50M invested in 2019-20. SEC filings show 19,737,553 Class B shares, about 15% (our arithmetic), worth roughly $1.65B at the first-day close.

The brief's phrase 'Newsmax's dealings with the administration' implies favourable treatment. The documented record shows Newsmax opposing the FCC's Nexstar-Tegna approval and leaving the Pentagon under Hegseth's rules; its defamation settlements were private disputes.
Heritage's deal with Daibes was finalized in December 2022 for $45M for a quarter stake (FDD, Daily Beast). The indictment's 2023 joint-venture language refers to the same relationship.
C73 could not read the Free Beacon jet article. Its claim is that Sheikh Sultan is an HBJ confidant and business partner, from an anonymous source; it does not say Heritage owns the jet.
denials_and_context: Heritage says it operates independently of any government, invests only for value, and has no editorial or management control over media holdings. Its lawyers say Sheikh Sultan bought the Newsmax stake for profit and not on behalf of Qatar.
Heritage's lawyers say Sheikh Sultan had no relationship with IS EG Halal and did not know of the property overlap.
Neither Sheikh Sultan nor Qatar was charged in the Menendez case. Doyle says he was unpaid and cooperated with law enforcement.
Newsmax denied softening its coverage of Qatar.
Zeldin's spokesperson declined to comment. A Senate Republican aide said he disclosed all that was required. Zeldin says the work required no FARA registration and involved no lobbying.
Daibes's lawyer says he ended the Javelin engagement in June 2025. The White House said the President alone decides pardons.
Network note: icij.org, sec.gov and oge.gov could not be fetched from this environment; findings rest on search-result text across several outlets.

leads.title: Hamad bin Jassim / Sheikh Sultan business partnership and the P4-HBJ jet
leads.why_connected: The Free Beacon (anonymous source) calls Sheikh Sultan an HBJ confidant and partner. That would join the Heritage/Menendez/Newsmax/Zeldin cluster to the Air Force One jet and the 666 Fifth episode (C66). Corporate records of shared vehicles would settle it.

leads.title: Heritage's Newsmax stake after the lockup: sales, value and Cayman structure
leads.why_connected: A ~15% block in a pro-Trump network worth ~$1.6B at listing. SEC Form 4/13D history would show whether a Qatari royal still holds it and how it voted.

leads.title: Hudson Edgewater Associates after Daibes's conviction
leads.why_connected: Heritage owns a quarter of Daibes's Edgewater holdings, including the IS EG Halal site. Forfeiture, sale or restructuring of the venture is unreported.

leads.title: Newsmax v. FCC over Nexstar-Tegna at the full Commission
leads.why_connected: A Qatari-royal-backed network is litigating against a Trump-endorsed merger approval by Carr's FCC. The full-Commission ruling was expected by end of 2026.

leads.title: Zeldin's 2026 annual disclosure and ethics-agreement compliance
leads.why_connected: The 2026 278e exists but its client and recusal entries were not readable here. It would show whether Heritage or other foreign clients persist through Diana Zeldin's work.
